chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the man has finished his Tawaf and prayed two cycles, let him go to Zamzam and draw from it a bucket or two buckets, and let him drink from it and pour it upon his head, back, and belly, and say: 'O Allah, make it beneficial knowledge, extensive sustenance, and healing from every illness and disease.' Then he should return to the Black Stone.

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْهُ: O Allah, make it (a supplication formula)
key_terms.ذَنُوب: A bucket or vessel used for drawing water
key_terms.زَمْزَم: Zamzam, the sacred well in Mecca
key_terms.طَوَاف: Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and ritual action after completing Tawaf in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the Sunnah of drinking and pouring Zamzam water immediately after the two rak'ahs of Tawaf, emphasizing its spiritual utility for both physical and metaphysical well-being. The specific supplication highlights the holistic nature of divine provision, linking intellectual nourishment ('useful knowledge') with material sustenance and comprehensive healing, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the barakah (blessing) of sacred sites. This practice is often cited by scholars to support the permissibility and virtue of consuming Zamzam water for specific intentions (niyyah) beyond mere thirst.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man is free from his Tawaaf, and he has Prayed two Cycles, so let him go to Zamzam and let him draw from it, a bucket or two buckets, and let him drink from it, and let him pour it upon his head, and his back, and his belly, and he should be saying, ‘O Allahazwj! Make to be to a beneficial knowledge, and an extensive sustenance, and a healing from every illness and disease. Then he should return to the Black Stone’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when a man completes Tawaf and the two Rak‘at salat (prayer), he should go to Zamzam. He should take one or two containers full of water, drink, pour on his head, back and belly and say, ‘O Allah, make it useful knowledge, abundant sustenance and a cure for all illnesses and deficiencies,’ and then go back to the Black Stone.’”
